## Objective
- Complete and validate the existing playable browser game about Marcus’s return to Harbor City to investigate his brother’s death and seek revenge.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game, not just a design or plan; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Include an open city, story missions, free roaming, vehicles, swimming, weapons, and climbing, with a realistic AAA/UE5 feel.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing repository as a stylized 2D browser canvas game; this approach does not achieve AAA/UE5 realism.
- Story progression covers South Market, three crew leads, Harbor Precinct, and Crown Warehouse.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI, HUD, title/pause/ending screens, and responsive styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Completed `game.js` with city rendering, characters, vehicles, markers, minimap, combat, dialogue and mission progression, keyboard/mouse/touch controls, and game loop.
- Added shotgun damage/cooldown and made enemies only pursue during the final mission.
- Confirmed the local server responds and system Chromium can capture the page.

### Active
- Fix and validate the stylesheet, then test the game in-browser.

### Blocked
- `style.css` parsing stops after `.vignette`; browser inspection showed only nine CSS rules were loaded, leaving later UI unstyled. The gradient declaration likely has an unmatched parenthesis.
- `playwright-cli open` cannot launch its expected Chromium installation; system Chromium is available and can be used via `playwright-core`.

## Next Move
1. Fix the malformed `.vignette` CSS declaration and confirm all stylesheet rules load.
2. Run `node --check game.js` after the latest edits.
3. Use system Chromium/Playwright to test start, gameplay interactions, and check for console errors; inspect a fresh screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, controls, and progression.
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `style.css`: Game presentation; currently has a CSS parse issue.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The previous `node --check game.js` passed before the most recent small gameplay edits; the malformed stylesheet was found in the subsequent browser inspection.
